title: Extending prescribed fiber colimit cocones over one simplex
statement:
Use simplicial sets, nerves, quasicategories, coherent transformations and colimiting cocones as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a universe containing the small categories below. Fix an integer $n\geq1$ and the ordered category $[n]=\{0<\cdots<n\}$. Let $V:[n]\to\mathrm{Cat}$ be a strict functor to small ordinary categories. Define $K_V$ to have objects $(r,x)$ with $x\in V(r)$ and morphisms $(r,x)\to(s,y)$ the pairs $(r\leq s,\alpha:V(r\leq s)(x)\to y)$, composed by $(s\leq t,\beta)(r\leq s,\alpha)=(r\leq t,\beta V(s\leq t)(\alpha))$. Let $P_V$ contain disjoint full copies of $K_V$ and $[n]$, with $\operatorname{Hom}_{P_V}((r,x),s)$ a singleton for $r\leq s$ and empty otherwise, and with no arrows from $[n]$ to $K_V$; compose mixed arrows using the order and the displayed projection. Let $\pi_V:P_V\to[n]$ send $(r,x)$ to $r$ and the second-copy vertex $s$ to $s$. Put $\Delta^n=N([n])$ and let $\partial\Delta^n$ be the union of its proper faces. Form the simplicial subset
$$B_V=N(K_V)\ \cup\ (N\pi_V)^{-1}(\partial\Delta^n)\ \subseteq N(P_V).$$
Let $\mathcal E$ be a quasicategory and $F:B_V\to\mathcal E$ a simplicial map. For every vertex $r$, the full subcategory of $P_V$ on $V(r)$ and the second-copy vertex $r$ is $V(r)$ with a final object adjoined. Suppose its restriction under $F$ induces a colimiting coherent cocone on $F|_{N(V(r))}$: the transformation is obtained by precomposing with $N(V(r))\times\Delta^1\to N(V(r)^{\triangleright})$ which sends time $0$ to $V(r)$ and time $1$ to the new final vertex. Then there exists a simplicial map $\widetilde F:N(P_V)\to\mathcal E$ with $\widetilde F|_{B_V}=F$. The entire boundary map and every already prescribed vertex cocone are fixed, not merely equivalent after restriction. No colimit-preservation property of $V(r\leq s)$ is required.

source.place: Kerodon Lemma 7.3.4.5 (02ZR), restricted to base $\Delta^n$, subset $\partial\Delta^n$ with $n\geq1$, target map $\mathcal E\to\Delta^0$, and the nerve of the displayed split Grothendieck projection. Its cocartesian lifts are $(r\leq s,\mathrm{id})$. The relative join is the nerve of the displayed collage. The source fixes the entire boundary lift. The join/coherent-comma convention is that of the existing join-cone calculus, by opposites. Read online; not archived. This is a Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag.

proof.text: Put $S=\Delta^n$, $X=N(K_V)$ and $Y=N(P_V)$, with their projections to $S$. Let $V^+(r)$ be $V(r)$ with one new final object $*_r$; extend each $V(r\leq s)$ by $*_r\mapsto *_s$ and send the unique arrows into $*_r$ to the unique arrows into $*_s$. This is a strict functor. Its Grothendieck category has exactly the arrows of $P_V$: arrows between old objects have the stated fiber component, arrows from an old object over $r$ to $*_s$ exist uniquely for $r\leq s$, arrows between new objects are the order arrows, and arrows from new to old objects do not exist. Hence the identification with $P_V$ commutes with composition and projection. Both $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ are cocartesian fibrations in the horn sense of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Indeed an inner horn in a nerve is filled by composing the consecutive arrows; the two composites on its overlap agree by associativity. For an arrow $r\leq s$, the chosen lift from $x$ is $(r\leq s,1_{V(r\leq s)x})$, with the same formula in $V^+$. Every arrow over $r\leq t$ factors uniquely through this lift followed by an arrow over $s\leq t$. In the defining $\Lambda_0^2$ lifting problem this factorization supplies the missing edge; in a $\Lambda_0^3$ problem the two possible composites agree by uniqueness, and for $m>3$ every missing face is forced by the same factorization and associativity (the remaining faces already lie in the horn). These are exactly the required cocartesian-edge horn fillers. The inclusion $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ preserves these lifts. More generally the $\Lambda_0^2$ condition for an edge $e$ gives existence of each factor through $e$. For uniqueness, if $ue=ve=h$, take the $\Lambda_0^3$ with vertices $(x,y,y,z)$ and edges $01=02=e$, $03=h$, $12=1_y$, $13=u$, $23=v$; its missing face forces $u=v$. Thus a cocartesian arrow $(r\leq s,\alpha)$ has the unique factorization property. Factoring the displayed chosen lift through it gives $\beta\alpha=1$; uniqueness applied to $(\alpha\beta)\alpha=\alpha$ gives $\alpha\beta=1$. Conversely an invertible component has the same unique factorization property and hence the horn fillers just described. Since $V(r)\subseteq V^+(r)$ preserves isomorphisms, $j$ preserves every cocartesian edge. All these simplicial sets fit in the chosen universe.

source.place: Opening construction of the relative join fibration; explicit ordinary Grothendieck-category verification replaces Lemma 5.2.3.17.

proof.text: For $Z=X,Y$ form $H_Z\to S$ with $m$-simplices $(\sigma:\Delta^m\to S,h:\Delta^m\times_S Z\to\mathcal E)$ as in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-exponential-restriction]. The projections are cartesian fibrations by the opposite dual of [lem-cbc-enhanced-relative-exponential]. To specify this dual precisely, reverse every ordinal using $\alpha^{\mathrm{rev}}(i)=m-\alpha(k-i)$ for $\alpha:[k]\to[m]$. This interchanges first and last horns and identifies the opposite of a pullback with the pullback of the opposites. Thus $Z^{\mathrm{op}}\to S^{\mathrm{op}}$ is cartesian. Apply the cited theorem with target $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ and take opposites: its resulting cocartesian fibration becomes the stated cartesian fibration $H_Z\to S$. The degreewise identification sends $(\sigma,h)$ to the reversed map on the reversed pullback. Equivalences are preserved under reversal since their two inverse-triangle witnesses reverse. Its edge criterion therefore says that an edge of $H_Z$ is cartesian precisely when its associated map $\Delta^1\times_S Z\to\mathcal E$ sends every cocartesian edge to an equivalence. Restriction $R:H_Y\to H_X$ preserves cartesian edges: by Step 1, the pullback of $j$ carries cocartesian edges to cocartesian edges, so the restriction of such a map retains this property. Here the pullbacks along an edge are exactly the Grothendieck categories of the restricted two-term strict functors, with the same invertible-component criterion. The fibers identify degreewise with $\operatorname{Fun}(Z_r,\mathcal E)$, since a constant base simplex gives $\Delta^m\times Z_r$. Finally [lem-coef-infinity-relative-exponential-restriction] applies to $j$, which is degreewise injective, and supplies the inner-fibration property of $R$.

source.place: Relative functor categories and their cartesian projections, as in equation 7.22; the isofibration assertion is used only as an inner fibration.

proof.text: Write $Q=F|_X$. Define $b:S\to H_X$ by $b(\sigma)=(\sigma,Q\circ\operatorname{pr}_X)$ for each simplex $\sigma:\Delta^m\to S$. Define $a:\partial S\to H_Y$ by $a(\sigma)=(\sigma,F\circ\operatorname{pr}_Y)$; this is defined because $\operatorname{pr}_Y$ has image in $(N\pi_V)^{-1}(\partial S)\subseteq B_V$. Pulling back along a face or degeneracy just precomposes the displayed maps, so $a,b$ are simplicial and $Ra=b|_{\partial S}$. The projection of $b$ is the identity of $S$. At a vertex $r$, the strict fiber of $X$ is $N(V(r))$ and that of $Y$ is $N(V(r)^{\triangleright})$. The latter equals the right join cone on $N(V(r))$: every chain consists of an initial chain of old objects followed by new final vertices, with precisely the faces and degeneracies of the join. The vertex $a(r)$ is the actual prescribed map on this fiber, not a replacement chosen up to equivalence.

source.place: Unwinding the relative-exponential adjunction and the given lifting square (7.21).

proof.text:
Let $r=0$ and write $c=a(0):N(V(0))^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal E$. The vertex $0$ lies in $\partial\Delta^n$ because $n\geq1$. The induced coherent cocone is precisely the cocone in the hypothesis: on $N(V(0))\times\Delta^1$ the time-zero vertices remain old and the time-one vertices become the new final object. Hence it is colimiting. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocone-restriction-initial] with $K=N(V(0))$. For every $t$ in the fiber $(H_Y)_0=\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleright},\mathcal E)$ it gives the equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{(H_Y)_0}(a(0),t)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{(H_X)_0}(Ra(0),Rt).$$
The target cone $t$ may have any base diagram, exactly as required by that node. This establishes relative initiality in the entire fiber, rather than only initiality in the subcategory with base $Q|_K$ fixed.

source.place: Condition (*) gives fiberwise relative initiality, Proposition 7.1.6.13 (colimit dual).

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cartesian-initial-boundary-lift] with $\mathcal A=H_Y$, $\mathcal D=H_X$, base $S$, and the square $(a,b)$ of Step 3. Step 2 gives both cartesian fibrations, the inner fibration $R$, and preservation of cartesian edges. Step 4 gives every outgoing mapping-space equivalence required at the initial vertex. The dimension is positive. We obtain $\widetilde a:S\to H_Y$ with $\widetilde a|_{\partial S}=a$ and $R\widetilde a=b$ exactly. Its projection to $S$ is the identity because the projection of $b$ is the identity and $R$ lies over $S$.

source.place: Promotion through the cartesian family and boundary filling: Proposition 7.1.5.19(2), Corollary 7.1.5.17.

proof.text: Uncurry this section explicitly. For an $m$-simplex $y:\Delta^m\to Y$ put $\sigma=\pi_Vy$ and write $\widetilde a(\sigma)=(\sigma,h_\sigma)$. Set $\widetilde F(y)=h_\sigma(\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^m},y)$, evaluated on the diagonal simplex in $\Delta^m\times_S Y$. The simplicial identities for $\widetilde a$ say $h_{\sigma\alpha}=h_\sigma\circ(\alpha\times\operatorname{id})$ on the corresponding pullback, so this rule commutes with every simplicial operator. The equality $R\widetilde a=b$ implies $\widetilde F|_X=Q$; the equality $\widetilde a|_{\partial S}=a$ implies $\widetilde F=F$ on $(N\pi_V)^{-1}(\partial S)$. These two subsets have union $B_V$, and the maps agree on their intersection because they both equal the original $F$ there. Thus $\widetilde F|_{B_V}=F$ exactly. Every vertex fiber lies in that boundary preimage, so every prescribed fiber cocone, including every higher simplex in it, is fixed. The construction used the given colimit at vertex $0$ and the hypothesis supplies it even when $V(0)$ is empty, in which case it means the specified apex is initial. No transition functor was asked to preserve a colimit.

source.place: Uncurrying the solution of equation 7.21 and checking exact agreement on both pieces of the prescribed union.

lean.statement: theorem fiber_cocone_simplex_extension (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (V : simplexIndex.{u} n ⥤ Cat.{u, u}) {E : SSet.{u}} [E.Quasicategory] (F : (simplexBoundaryCollage V : SSet) ⟶ E) (hcolim : ∀ r : simplexIndex n, ∃ c : (SSet.Enhanced.coconeCategory (simplexFiberMap V r ≫ F)) _⦋0⦌, (∃ b : (simplexBoundaryCollage V : SSet) _⦋0⦌, b.1 = (nerveMap (collageRight (I := simplexIndex n) (U := V))).app (op ⦋0⦌) (ComposableArrows.mk₀ r) ∧ c.1.1 = F.app _ b) ∧ SSet.Enhanced.IsColimiting (simplexFiberMap V r ≫ F) c ∧ ∀ (m : ℕ) (s : (nerve (V.obj r)) _⦋m⦌) (a : (Δ[1] : SSet.{u}) _⦋m⦌), ∃ b : (simplexBoundaryCollage V : SSet) _⦋m⦌, b.1 = (collageFiberPrism V r).app (op ⦋m⦌) (s, a) ∧ (SSet.Enhanced.coconeHomotopy (simplexFiberMap V r ≫ F) c).app (op ⦋m⦌) (s, a) = F.app _ b) : ∃ Fbar : nerve (Collage (simplexIndex n) V) ⟶ E, (simplexBoundaryCollage V).ι ≫ Fbar = F
lean.note: Uses the published canonical Collage and collageFiberPrism helpers. The hypothesis identifies the supplied colimiting cocone with the prescribed apex and entire prism, including empty fibers; subtype witnesses only express membership in the prescribed union. The boundary is Mathlib boundary transported by stdSimplex.isoNerve.
